label: GO step, except choosing a1 after a rewarded trial (strongest for a2 after no reward)
explanation: Fires only at GO; it is silent at D1 and D2 (2 D2 activations in total). At GO it is active when the agent is choosing a2 (model_act==2: 78% firing rate, 88% of mass) or when the previous trial went unrewarded. It is essentially silent on the GO steps where the agent picks a1 after a rewarded trial. Rates by subgroup: a2 after no reward 98% active, carrying the largest activations (57% of mass); a2 after reward 67%; a1 after no reward 56% with small activations. Activations grow over runs of consecutive unrewarded a2 trials and are small after rewarded ones, so magnitude tracks a2 choice combined with recent lack of reward. Its strongest correlate is a strongly negative policy logit (choice < -8.9: 84% active). The only inputs used are the agent own GO choice (computed at that step) and the observed previous reward, so no future variables. Dev: P 0.73, R 0.98, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.995. The simpler GO & model_act==2 gives F1 0.80.

issues: The factual claims hold up. The feature fires only at GO (196958 of 196960 active steps; 2 at D2, 0 at D1). Dev firing rates by subgroup: a2 after no reward 97.8% active with 57% of activation mass; a2 after reward 67%; a1 after no reward 56%; a1 after reward 2.6%. Test scores of the original predicate reproduce: P 0.739, R 0.985, F1 0.844, mass recall 0.996.

Systematic false-positive class 1, a2 chosen after a REWARDED trial that reached S1. The feature is almost silent here: dev precision 0.066 on 12204 steps, mass recall 0.0015. The same pattern after a rewarded trial that reached S2 is 75% active. A rewarded rare a2->S1 trial is also mostly silent: prev_common==0 gives precision 0.25. The label's 'a2 after a reward' bucket hides this split.

Systematic false-positive class 2, a1 chosen after an unrewarded trial. Firing depends on the previous trial: prev_action==2 gives 99.5% active, while prev_action==1 with prev_state==1 gives only 26.5% (15k steps). The '56% active' figure averages a near-always class with a near-never class.

Taken together, the feature is suppressed whenever the last outcome was evidence for S1 (rewarded at S1), not only when a1 follows a reward. It fires when the choice or recent evidence favours a2/S2. This fits the reported correlation with a negative choice logit.

Remaining graded noise: a2 after long rewarded S2 streaks is about 44-56% active and smaller in magnitude. This is graded rather than a clean class, and the explanation already says magnitude is small after rewarded trials.
No future variables are used, either in the original predicate or in the refinement (prev_state is observed at D2 of the previous trial).
skeptic.revised_label: GO step when the choice or the last outcome points to a2/S2: fires when choosing a2 (except right after a reward at S1) or after an unrewarded trial (except when choosing a1 after an unrewarded visit to S1); strongest for a2 after no reward
